story: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price M&M to move about ±5.9%, roughly 3,247 to 3,655. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 60% of the time.
Options are cheap compared with how much M&M has actually been moving: they price 25.2% a year while the last month realised 37.6%.
M&M futures trade 1.4 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 0.5% a year, lower than almost any day this past year: hedgers or short sellers are leaning on the futures.
M&M has actually been moving about 2.37% a day this past month: on the high side for it against the past year.

iv.simple: Options on M&M are priced for moves of about 1.59% a day. That is normal for M&M compared with the past year.
iv.analyst: 30-day constant-maturity ATM IV 25.2%: 44th percentile of 1 year, 25th of all days since 2019-01-01.

vrp.simple: Options are cheap compared with how much M&M has actually been moving: they price 25.2% a year while the last month realised 37.6%.
vrp.analyst: IV30 - RV21 = -12.4 vol points, 3rd percentile of the past year. Since 2019-01-01, IV30 was above the volatility that actually followed over the next 21 sessions on 61% of days: option sellers are usually paid a premium for carrying the risk, and the gap is what that premium looks like today.

term.simple: Near and far options on M&M are priced about the same: nothing special is expected soon.

skew.simple: Calls and puts the same distance from the price cost about the same (gap -0.4 vol points): no strong demand for either protection or upside. Against the past year, that gap is normal for M&M.
skew.analyst: 25-delta risk reversal -0.35 vol pts (front month), 67th percentile of the past year. More negative = more demand for downside insurance relative to upside.

realised.simple: M&M has actually been moving about 2.37% a day this past month: on the high side for it against the past year.
realised.analyst: RV21 37.6% (89th percentile of the past year), RV5 17.9%, RV63 28.7%; RV5/RV63 compression at the 22nd percentile.

oi.simple: For the 2026-12-29 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 3,600 (+4.3% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 3,300 (-4.3%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
oi.analyst: Front-expiry PCR (OI) 0.73; all-expiry OI PCR at the 55th percentile of the past year. Today's change: calls +221,200, puts +41,000 (OI units, i.e. shares or index quantity). A high PCR in India mostly reflects put writing, so it is read as crowding, not as a signal.

futures.simple: M&M futures trade 1.4 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 0.5% a year, lower than almost any day this past year: hedgers or short sellers are leaning on the futures.
futures.analyst: Near-month basis +1.4, annualised carry 0.5% (9th percentile of the past year; its 1-year median 6.0%). Last 5 sessions (price x OI, same contracts day to day): Long build-up, Long unwinding, Short covering, Long unwinding, Short build-up. Build-up labels describe what happened to positions; they do not say who is right.

move.simple: Until 2026-12-29 (32 days), options price M&M to move about ±5.9%, roughly 3,247 to 3,655. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 60% of the time.
move.analyst: ATM straddle / forward = 5.92% (forward 3,450.8). Scored on 1,951 days since 2019-01-01 against the official close on each expiry; a straddle is the market's mean absolute move, so about 57% inside is what a fair price would give.

notes.text: M&M has used 13% of its market-wide position limit (the ban starts at 95%).
